title.narrative: Provision of life saving WASH services to vulnerable drought affected IDPs and vulnerable host communities in Berdale district of Bay Region

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0) font-family: helvetica, sans-serif text-align: left background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255) text-decoration-color: initial display: inline !important"gtltspan style="line-height: 107% font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtSomalia is facing an unprecedented sixth consecutive season of below-average- April to June 2023 rains. The Protracted drought has claimed the lives and livelihoods of many. An estimated 8.25 million people require humanitarian assistance . The number of people affected by drought has more than doubled since the beginning of 2022. As per the 2023 HNO, drought induced displacement has increased fivefold since the beginning of 2022 with more than 1.3 million people displaced. Five regions including Banadir have received the biggest numbers of newly displaced people. About 95 per cent live in urban areas where humanitarian conditions are dire and where spikes in displacement have strained the capacity of the humanitarian system to cope. The displaced have joined newly formed IDP sites or existing over-crowded settlements further putting immense pressure on the limited basic services. lt/spangtlt/spangtltspan style="font-family: Calibri, sans-serif background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255) color: rgb(0, 0, 0)"gtA new report released by the Federal Ministry of Health Human Services, WHO and UNICEF suggests that an estimated 43,000 excess deaths might have occurred in 2022 in Somalia resulting from a deepening drought when compared with 2017 and 2018 drought crisis. Half of these deaths might have occurred among children under the age of 5.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0) font-family: helvetica, sans-serif text-align: left background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255) text-decoration-color: initial display: inline !important"gtltspan style="line-height: 107% font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtWater shortages are at critical levels exposing vulnerable people to additional risks. Water prices are six times higher than at the beginning of 2022 and are likely to remain high. ltbrgt Increasing fltspan style="font-family:"gtood insecurity and declining water availability and quality have led to uninterrupted outbreaks of AWD/Choleralt/spangt ltspan style="font-family:"gtin 26 drought affected districts since 2022 including Bay region especially Baidoa/Berdale districts) As of 26ltsupgtthlt/supgt March 2023, a total of 3,428 cholera cases including 14 deaths (CFR: 0.5%) where report have been reported from 27 of the 74 drought affected districts.lt/spangt
lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbr style="border-color: inherit font-family: helvetica, sans-serif outline-color: initial color: rgb(0, 0, 0) text-align: left background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255) text-decoration-color: initial"gtltspan style="line-height: 107% font-family:"gtIn this project, ARD is planning to provide life-saving WASH services to 10,000 beneficiaries (1500 men, 5500 women, 1200 boys and 1800 girls) for Berdale drought affected IDPs and host communities with recognition of people with disabilities and the most vulnerable population through the provision of emergency safe water drinking with water vouchers system for 50 days period for a total of 7500 people (900 HHs), Rehabilitation of 12 flood-proof shallow wells. ARD will also construct 20 emergency latrines in Berdale IDPs 5 of it for PLWD. A total of 88 HHs will benefit from access to the sanitation, 800 Households will benefit from hygiene kit distribution and hygiene awareness, Chlorination of 12 Shallow wells and WASH committees will be established in addition to carrying out environmental sanitation services to all project target locations especially IDP camps to improve all preventive measures against the risks of AWD/cholera outbreaks in Bedale district.lt/spangt
